_note: The OEM and supplier register: who the fifty products in the founder's sourcing catalogue of 2 October 2026 are from, what each supplier and offer states about itself, what selling each in South Africa would need beyond what the catalogue lists, and where each would fit MyThuso — if anywhere. The founder's words: "lets have this on the OEM/Supplier so that we know who these are from." It is a back-office record and nothing else: read by the Control Tower's Catalogue · Suppliers & OEMs screen behind a dynamic import, never by the shop, which is unbranded on purpose (shop.json, _brandNote). Every fact about a supplier or an offer is the catalogue's, and the catalogue was prepared by an AI; none of it is verified, and the register says what was tried.
_statusWhy: In the tree, held by scripts/check-suppliers.mjs and tests/suppliers.spec.ts on both viewports. Built is not procured: nothing has been ordered, no sample requested and no supplier contacted.

decided.words: lets have this on the OEM/Supplier so that we know who these are from.

_platformsWhy: The register is read in the Control Tower, which is a web surface; neither phone has a back office. So there is no generator and no Swift or Kotlin copy — a copy nobody renders is a copy nobody would notice drifting.

source.title: Healthcare & Medical Products Master Catalogue — Verified B2B Procurement Edition: Connected Medical Equipment, Diagnostic Telehealth & Nutritional Supplements
source.preparedBy: "AI Mode Sourcing Expert" — an AI-prepared document
source.itsOwnChecklist: Medical equipment: FCC Part 15/22/24, PTCRB and CE-RED for the radio; CE MDR (EU) 2017/745, FDA 510(k) and ISO 13485 for the medical function. Supplements: cGMP (21 CFR Part 111), ISO 22000 and HACCP, a lot certificate of analysis for heavy metals, microbes and assay, and FDA or EFSA labelling. It recommends Alibaba Trade Assurance, binding specification sheets and Incoterms, and physical samples before production.
source._itsOwnChecklistWhy: Kept because it is the catalogue's own list, and because every item on it is American or European. None of them is a South African approval, which is what saFit below is for.
source._urlPatternWhy: The catalogue's links were "View Product Details & Inquire (ID: …)". The address is built from the ID by this one pattern, so a link is never typed twice and never carries anything but a public product ID.

saFitLevels.label: Paperwork first
saFitLevels.sentence: Lawful to bring in once the licences and approvals it needs exist. Today none of them does.

saFitLevels.label: Only with conditions met
saFitLevels.sentence: Possible only if its data can come into Thuso instead of its maker's cloud, or a flagged claim is cleared or dropped — on top of the paperwork.

saFitLevels.label: Not as offered
saFitLevels.sentence: As the catalogue offers it, it carries a claim that is unlawful to repeat here. It could be sold only as a different product, relabelled and registered, if at all.

_saFitLevelsWhy: The level is worked out, never typed: a claim whose severity blocks the offer makes it not as offered; otherwise readings that go to the supplier's cloud, or any flagged claim, make it conditional; otherwise it is paperwork first. apps/web/src/lib/suppliers.ts holds the rule and scripts/check-suppliers.mjs asks the same function, so the filter, the badge and the check cannot disagree.

claimSeverities.label: Unlawful to repeat
claimSeverities.sentence: A claim to treat, prevent or reduce the risk of a disease, or to modify a bodily function, for a product not registered as a medicine. SAHPRA calls these high-risk claims, which an unregistered complementary medicine may not make, and a food label may make no medicinal claim at all. Repeating one to a patient would be MyThuso making it.

claimSeverities.label: Needs its own clearance
claimSeverities.sentence: A diagnostic or monitoring claim the device would have to be classified and licensed for, separately from what it does at its simplest.

claimSeverities.label: Unsafe to repeat untested
claimSeverities.sentence: A safety promise a person would rely on — a fall noticed, a dose locked away, an alarm that wakes them — with no evidence offered that it works.

claimSeverities.label: Misleading here
claimSeverities.sentence: A certification or compliance claim that does not mean, in South Africa, what a reader would take it to mean.

_radiosWhy: Which requirements a radio brings is decided here once, from the words the catalogue uses for it. GPS is left out: a receiver that only listens to satellites transmits nothing to approve. Ethernet and USB are wires.
_deviceClassesWhy: One vocabulary of SAHPRA classes, the shop's, because an offer that could supply a listing must be read in the same words as the listing. scripts/check-suppliers.mjs fails an offer whose class the shop does not define, and a shop candidate whose class differs from the listing it would supply.

uploads.label: To the phone or tablet beside it
Runs our software; sends what that sends

popia.flagSentence: Its readings go to the supplier's own cloud, outside South Africa. That is a cross-border transfer of health information under POPIA section 72, needing the Information Regulator's prior authorisation under section 57(1)(d) where the destination is not adequately protected.
popia.acceptableOnlyIf: Acceptable only if its readings can come into Thuso instead — the device talking to the person's phone or to MyThuso, and the supplier's cloud switched off — and that is confirmed in writing before any order.
popia.unstatedSentence: The catalogue does not say where its data goes. That is the first question to ask, before price.

requirements.label: SAHPRA medical device establishment licence
requirements.instrument: Medicines and Related Substances Act 101 of 1965, section 22C(1)(b) and (6); guideline SAHPGL-MD-06 v3 (8 March 2023)
requirements.what: Nobody may import, distribute or wholesale a medical device or IVD of class B, C or D without this licence, and each licence carries the list of products it covers. Only class A devices that are neither sterile nor measuring are exempt.
requirements.missing: MyThuso holds no establishment licence, and no importer has been named who does.

requirements.label: The device's class, confirmed
requirements.instrument: Regulations relating to Medical Devices and IVDs, GN R1515 of 9 December 2016; guideline SAHPGL-MD-04 v5 (27 February 2025)
requirements.what: The class shown here is our reading of the classification guideline. The class of a particular model is the licence holder's to confirm, and individual registration waits on a call-up SAHPRA has not yet published.
requirements.missing: Nobody has confirmed a class for any of these models.

requirements.label: ICASA type approval
requirements.instrument: Electronic Communications Act 36 of 2005, section 35; Type Approval Regulations 2013
requirements.what: No radio equipment may be supplied, sold or used in South Africa until ICASA has approved it, licence-exempt short-range radios included. A LoRa radio must use a South African short-range band (863–870 or 915–919.4 MHz), not a setting made for another country.
requirements.missing: No model here has an ICASA approval MyThuso has seen.

requirements.label: RICA registration of every SIM
requirements.instrument: Regulation of Interception of Communications and Provision of Communication-related Information Act 70 of 2002, sections 40 and 62C
requirements.what: A SIM card is not activated until the person or company it is issued to is recorded and verified. A device with its own SIM needs a South African SIM registered to somebody — a foreign SIM roaming here permanently is a question for the operator.
requirements.missing: No SIM is registered for any device, and who would hold them has not been decided.
requirements.confidence: read on the page; applying it to an internal SIM is our reading

requirements.label: NRCS letter of authority, if the charger is in scope
requirements.instrument: Compulsory specification VC 8055 for electrical and electronic apparatus (GN R89 of 2009, amended by GN 835 of 2014)
requirements.what: Battery chargers, adaptors and IT equipment in the specification's scope need a letter of authority before they are imported or sold. Whether a medical device's own charger is in scope could not be confirmed, so each product needs a scope ruling from NRCS.
requirements.missing: No scope ruling has been asked for and no letter of authority is held.
requirements.confidence: not confirmed — the scope for medical equipment is the open question

requirements.label: Listed electronic product under the Hazardous Substances Act
requirements.instrument: Hazardous Substances Act 15 of 1973; Schedule of Listed Electronic Products, R1302 of 14 June 1991
requirements.what: Diagnostic ultrasound, electrocardiographs, physiological monitors and non-invasive blood pressure monitors are listed Group III electronic products, whose importer needs a licence. Whether that licence is still issued alongside the establishment licence is a question for Radiation Control.
requirements.missing: Nobody has asked Radiation Control, and no licence is held.
requirements.confidence: the listing read on the page; whether a licence is still issued is not confirmed

requirements.label: A clinical scope and the training for it
requirements.instrument: The scope of practice of the person who would use it
requirements.what: Diagnostic ultrasound is a sonographer's or a doctor's work, and fitting a hearing aid an audiologist's; in 2013 the HPCSA warned that selling hearing aids without its registration breaks the law. No instrument found lets a registered nurse do either.
requirements.missing: No scope decision has been made and nobody in MyThuso is trained or registered for it.
requirements.confidence: the HPCSA warning read on the page; the nurse's scope is not confirmed

requirements.label: POPIA: health information sent abroad
requirements.instrument: Protection of Personal Information Act 4 of 2013, sections 26, 57(1)(d) and 72
requirements.what: Health information is special personal information. Sending it to a third party in another country is allowed only under section 72's conditions, and where that country's protection is not adequate the Regulator must authorise it first.
requirements.missing: No transfer has been assessed, no authorisation sought, and no DPIA exists.

requirements.label: POPIA: biometric information
requirements.instrument: Protection of Personal Information Act 4 of 2013, sections 1, 26 and 27
requirements.what: A palm-vein template is biometric information, which is special personal information. It may be processed only on a section 27 ground such as consent, and never because it is convenient.
requirements.missing: MyThuso takes no biometrics and has no ground to start.

requirements.label: SAHPRA: complementary medicine (Category D)
requirements.instrument: General Regulations, GN R859 of 25 August 2017; guideline 7.02 and the health supplements guideline 7.04
requirements.what: A health supplement is a Category D complementary medicine. Until it is called up for registration it may be sold only with the prescribed words on its label: "This unregistered medicine has not been evaluated by the SAHPRA for its quality, safety or intended use." Each ingredient has its permitted claims and its maximum daily amount.
requirements.missing: No label, ingredient list or claim has been checked against the guideline, and nobody holds the product's dossier.

requirements.label: Only low-risk claims
requirements.authority: SAHPRA and the Department of Health
requirements.instrument: SAHPRA guideline 7.02 (December 2021); Foodstuffs, Cosmetics and Disinfectants Act 54 of 1972, labelling regulations R146 of 2010, regulation 13(g)
requirements.what: An unregistered complementary medicine may make only low-risk claims — general health, health maintenance, relief of minor symptoms with no disease named. A claim to treat, prevent or reduce the risk of a disease is high-risk and may bring an individual call-up and an order to stop selling; on a food label any medicinal claim is prohibited outright.
requirements.missing: No claim on any of these products has been reviewed, and several are high-risk as offered.

beforeAnyOrder.label: A physical sample
beforeAnyOrder.sentence: In the hands of whoever would use it — a nurse for a handheld, a household for a pendant — tested against the listing it would supply, before any production order.

beforeAnyOrder.label: A binding specification sheet
beforeAnyOrder.sentence: The exact model, firmware, radio bands and accessories, signed as part of the order, so the thing delivered is the thing tested.

beforeAnyOrder.label: The regulatory documents themselves
beforeAnyOrder.sentence: Certificates for every claimed approval, checked against the issuer's public register — a CE certificate's notified body, an FDA listing, an ISO certificate's issuer — never accepted as a picture on a listing.

beforeAnyOrder.label: A certificate of analysis for each lot
beforeAnyOrder.sentence: For anything taken by mouth: heavy metals, microbes and assay, from a laboratory that is not the supplier's, before the founder decides whether supplements are sold at all.

beforeAnyOrder.label: The data flow, in writing
beforeAnyOrder.sentence: Where every reading, position and recording goes, who holds it, in which country, and whether it can come into Thuso instead. For a device with a radio this comes before price.

beforeAnyOrder.label: The business licence
beforeAnyOrder.sentence: The supplier's business licence and registration number, so that two names that look alike are known to be one company or two, and a trading firm names the factory.

beforeAnyOrder.label: Who imports and who holds the licence
beforeAnyOrder.sentence: A South African importer or distributor holding the SAHPRA medical device establishment licence and the ICASA approvals, named before the order — MyThuso holds neither.

beforeAnyOrder.label: Incoterms and Trade Assurance
beforeAnyOrder.sentence: Who pays freight, duty and VAT and when the goods become MyThuso's (FOB, CIF or DDP), written into the order. The catalogue recommends this too.

attempts.method: An automated read of the product page at the catalogue's address, with a desktop browser's user agent.
attempts.result: Alibaba answered all six with the same interstitial of about ninety kilobytes — its slider captcha ("baxia", "punish") — and no product content. Nothing on any of the six pages could be read, so nothing was confirmed or contradicted.

attempts.result: Where it is recorded, the search engine's index held a listing at that ID under a title matching the catalogue's. An index entry can be weeks old; it says the listing existed, not what it says or costs today.

attempts.result: What was found is recorded on the supplier. A company's own website says what it says about itself; none of it is a business licence.

refusals.why: The catalogue's own checklist is American and European. What South Africa needs — SAHPRA, ICASA, RICA, NRCS, POPIA — is listed per offer with what is missing, and today it is all of it.

saFit.uploadsStated: Location and readings go over its own 4G SIM to a server; the maker's own pages say health data is sent to its server in real time.

claims.claim: Medical-grade temperature, heart rate and SpO2 from a wrist watch
claims.why: Calling a watch's readings medical is a monitoring claim. It needs the watch classified and licensed as a measuring device, and no accuracy study is offered for any of the three readings.

scope.why: The shop's fall-detection pendant raises an alert through the phone it is paired with; this is a watch that measures three vital signs and reports them to its maker's server. It is neither the pendant nor a validated measuring device, and the shop sells no watch.
